record.gold_sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) AS n_projects, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day', startDate, endDate)),1) AS avg_duration_days FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC-%' GROUP BY fundingScheme ORDER BY fundingScheme
record.reference_answer: Seven funding schemes carry an ERC- code, and their average durations fall into a long band and a short one. The long band is the main research grants, 5.7 to 6.7 years each: ERC-SyG averages 2446.0 days (99 projects), ERC-COG 2099.9 days (2254), ERC-STG 2083.3 days (2771) and ERC-ADG 2082.5 days (1584). The short band runs from about 1.6 to 1.8 years: ERC-LVG averages 656.2 days (5 projects), ERC-POC-LS 610.4 days (158) and ERC-POC 576.1 days (967). The five ERC-LVG grants are support awards to external publishing initiatives (OAPEN, SciPost, Europe PMC) rather than research projects. No ERC project has a missing start or end date, so all 7838 of them are included.
record.notes: Group set is pinned in the question text to the ERC- scheme code, and the text also pins the metric to subtraction (end date minus start date), because an inclusive endpoint count returns exactly +1.0 day on all seven rows and results_match compares at 1e-6. Boundedness checked on two channels. (1) Scheme string: SELECT DISTINCT fundingScheme FROM project WHERE lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%erc%' OR lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%research council%' returns exactly the seven ERC- codes (ERC-ADG, ERC-COG, ERC-LVG, ERC-POC, ERC-POC-LS, ERC-STG, ERC-SyG). (2) Programme channel, the near-miss: SELECT p.fundingScheme, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day',p.startDate,p.endDate)),1) FROM project p JOIN legal_basis lb ON lb.projectID=p.id WHERE lower(lb.title) LIKE '%european research council%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 returns those seven rows unchanged PLUS an eighth group, CSA | 12 | 813.1 - ERC administration and communication contracts under the ERC programme part. The question's ERC- clause makes that eight-group reading unavailable. Duration is pinned to whole days deliberately: a months formula has two defensible variants (calendar month-boundary count vs days/30.44) giving different numbers. Null-date exposure is zero: the 12 corpus-wide projects with NULL startDate/endDate (structural finding sf-11) are all outside the ERC schemes - SUM(CASE WHEN startDate IS NULL OR endDate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 for every ERC- scheme, over 7838 ERC projects. ERC-LVG's five members were read directly (637529 ERC-EuropePMC-2-2014, 683680 ERC-OAPEN-2015, 810640 ERC-OAPEN-2017, 899590 ERC-SciPost-2019, 964352 ERC-OAPEN-2019) so the reference describes them from their titles, not by analogy to ERC-POC. Averages rounded to one decimal in the gold SQL. n_projects is context, not compared; answer_columns pins fundingScheme and avg_duration_days. No ranking asked or implied - sql_comparison=set.

findings.claim: 'Counted in days from its start date to its end date' admits an inclusive count as well as the subtraction the gold uses. The two differ by exactly one day on every row, and results_match compares at a 1e-6 tolerance, so the inclusive reading fails all seven rows rather than passing within slack.
findings.evidence: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(endDate - startDate),1), ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day', startDate, endDate)),1), ROUND(AVG(endDate - startDate + 1),1) FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 -> the inclusive column is +1.0 on all seven rows. Calendar-year contracts (e.g. 811195, 2018-01-01 to 2018-12-31) come out as 364 days under gold, which most readers would call a 365-day year.
findings.fix_direction: Four words pin it dead: '...to its end date (end date minus start date)'.
findings.ruling_why: Round 1: the inclusive-endpoint count is a losing but natural reading, and it misses every one of the seven rows against a 1e-6 tolerance rather than landing inside slack. Round 2: closed - '(end date minus start date)' names the arithmetic outright, and the critic's cold blind-solve from the new text returned the seven gold rows exactly.

judge_decisions.rationale: The cell is sound - the gold SQL, the seven-group set, the level evidence and every number reproduce, and the critic's blind solve landed on the gold row-for-row. All three defects are in the wording and the prose, none touches the gold SQL, the level, the subtype or the reference numbers, so the fix round is very likely to land.

The three upheld MIDs were the only things wrong, all three were bounded to wording, and all three closed on evidence the critic executed itself rather than on the drafter's assertion - including a cold blind-solve that lands on gold. gold_sql, answer_columns, level_evidence and every number are byte-identical, so the cell still measures what it measured: a genuine grouped-aggregate over a set of seven groups that a solver must pin before it can be scored. The carried-forward scans were re-measured, not trusted (7 schemes, 7838 projects, zero null dates). The remaining LOW - that the text now states its own predicate in schema vocabulary and reads more like a specification than a spoken question - is a phrasing observation, and the brief is explicit that phrasing alone is not a defect; it costs no discrimination here, since no condition can compute a per-scheme average either way.
